ai.description: This slender, worm-like snake reaches 20–25 cm. It is uniform dark brown to black with a pale snout and tail tip. Key features include a rounded head and a distinct, spine-tipped tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indotyphlops pammeces* is best distinguished by its exceptionally slender, thread-like body and a distinctive pale, white-colored snout tip that contrasts with its dark head.
ai.habitat: The South India Worm Snake inhabits moist deciduous forests and leaf litter in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The South India worm snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through soil and leaf litter in search of ant and termite larvae.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indotyphlops pammeces* is oviparous, typically laying a small clutch of 2–4 elongated eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indotyphlops pammeces* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at mid-to-high elevations in montane forest habitats.
